name: Tesamorelin
used_for: FDA-labeled for reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy; not indicated for general weight loss.

entries.text: Egrifta SV: labeled dose 1.4 mg (0.35 mL of reconstituted solution) injected subcutaneously once daily in the abdomen.
entries.population: HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat

entries.text: Egrifta WR: labeled dose 1.28 mg (0.16 mL of reconstituted solution) injected subcutaneously once daily in the abdomen; one vial is reconstituted to provide seven daily doses.
entries.population: HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta SV label: unreconstituted vials are stored at room temperature in the original box, protected from light.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta SV label: the solution is administered immediately after reconstitution; it is not stored, frozen or refrigerated, and unused solution is discarded.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta WR label: one reconstituted vial provides doses for 7 consecutive days, kept at room temperature (not frozen), and any remaining solution is discarded after 7 days.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta WR label: the bacteriostatic water diluent is discarded 28 days after first use.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Labels state the injection goes subcutaneously into the abdomen with rotating sites, avoiding the navel, scar tissue and bruises.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: Egrifta SV label: injection site reactions 17% vs 6% placebo, arthralgia 13% vs 11%, peripheral edema 6% vs 2%, and myalgia 6% vs 2%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Label warnings: increased risk of neoplasms (preexisting malignancy should be inactive), elevated IGF-1, fluid retention (edema, arthralgia, carpal tunnel syndrome), glucose intolerance (elevated HbA1c in 5% vs 1% placebo), hypersensitivity reactions (4%), and increased mortality in critically ill patients.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: Patient reviews of Egrifta WR are mixed: some describe reduced belly fat and easier movement, while others report no benefit, joint pain, hand numbness, preparation difficulty, and cost or supply problems.
Project Biohacking says tesamorelin mainly cuts deep belly fat (roughly 15 to 18 percent) and may preserve or modestly add lean mass, but warns that calling it a muscle builder oversells it.

Swolverine, a supplement brand's bodybuilding blog, argues tesamorelin raises natural growth hormone and IGF-1, targets stubborn abdominal fat while keeping lean tissue during a cut, and speeds recovery.

A longevity clinic's blog (the Evergreen Institute, which also promotes consultations) presents tesamorelin as a well-studied peptide that lowers visceral and liver fat and preserves muscle, and that clinicians may consider it beyond its HIV indication.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Egrifta SV (tesamorelin) for injection.
research.finding: Indicated to reduce excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy; not for general weight management.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Egrifta WR (tesamorelin) for injection.
research.finding: Same indication as Egrifta SV with a weekly-reconstitution format; long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established.

research.summary: Randomized placebo-controlled trial with safety extension of tesamorelin in HIV-infected patients with abdominal fat accumulation (Falutz et al., J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr).
research.finding: Visceral fat fell about 10.9% with tesamorelin versus 0.6% with placebo over 6 months; gains were lost after switching to placebo.

research.summary: Pooled analysis of two phase 3 trials (806 patients) of tesamorelin 2 mg daily versus placebo for 26 weeks, with a 26-week extension (Falutz et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Visceral fat decreased significantly versus placebo (treatment effect -15.4%) with lower triglycerides and no meaningful change in subcutaneous abdominal fat.
